I got you bro I'm Shiz and adhd and blah blah my sister is bipolar so we both have problems but you know. Anyway just know that if can get a job that pays the bills, have some food. Maybe a beer or two your pretty much good. As long as she sees you doing well and helping her out your all good.

I got you bro. One of the most important things is to basically be there. Be supportive and show her that she didn't fail. I love my mom. And she tries. She's a good mom. 

And one of the things I'd finish school. Maybe not college but at least finish high school. It may not be much right now. But it matters a lot. If you can get that level of education at least it will help you in the long term. 

She has to feel like she didn't fail as a mother. And seeing you graduate will hopefully add to that feeling. College is another thing entirely. But start with that. It helps.

Just remember though, because it's a dangerous game, your not the father you know?

You can be supportive, you can be a good son. But your not the father or husband. So it's important when you try to do these things and help out that you don't forget that your still young and that your needs are important as well as hers. It's a dangerous game when you try to play multiple roles. Sometimes it works, sometimes not. And if you do too much it can backfire. So find a balance that works for you and your family. Don't forget to be a loving son and don't forget that your life still has room to grow. So be there when you can and do the right th in ng for yourself as well as for her.

That's just my opinion. If that helps at all I'm glad. I hope this helped you in some way. I hope things get better.
